title: How To Make Your Front Door Kick-In Proof Like A VAULT
description:
A strong front door starts with what holds the lock to the house. Ray Kessler walks through the strike plate, fasteners, hinges, wood condition, reinforcement, deadbolt alignment, door construction, and nearby glass—so you can inspect the whole doorway before buying another expensive gadget.

Learn why a longer screw is only useful when it reaches sound framing, how to check a deadbolt with your own door open, and why easy two-finger operation matters. Ray also covers portable braces, rental-property limits, and a sensible Saturday work order.

The budget examples are planning illustrations, not quotes: the basic materials example totals $115, with optional upgrades discussed separately. Actual products, installation, labor, taxes, and repairs vary. No residential door is literally kick-in proof; the goal is to improve resistance while keeping everyday use and emergency exit practical. Follow the hardware manufacturer's instructions and get qualified help when the frame, glazing, or a rated door needs professional work.

THE ONE AFTERNOON DOOR
